FY 2025-26 was a year of decisive structural reset: exit from low-margin legacy transaction distribution, rebuild revenue base around contracted enterprise mandates, reset cost structure, strengthen balance sheet.

Revenue from operations at ₹35.01 Mn compares with ₹106.20 Mn in the previous year, reflecting deliberate run-off of legacy transaction distribution volumes and transition toward enterprise mandates with longer onboarding cycles but better tenure, margin and retention.
Total expenses reduced by 48.49% to ₹143.00 Mn from ₹277.63 Mn, reflecting sustained discipline on fixed overheads alongside lower variable costs.
Depreciation and amortisation fell to ₹8.65 Mn from ₹88.74 Mn as legacy platform and intangible assets substantially completed their amortisation cycle.
Loss for the year narrowed by 39.10% to ₹101.01 Mn.

outlook.statement: The Company remains focused on strengthening retailer economics, extending the platform's intelligence layer, and building durable value for the ecosystem it serves.

Industry shift from payment enablement toward broader retail and financial enablement plays to the Company's capability; enterprises moving spend toward structured, measurable programmes on compliant platforms favours organised, technology-led operators — a structural opportunity for the Group.

The Board views the opportunity set as the strongest in several years, driven by formalisation of unorganised retail, deepening earnings per outlet, large under-digitised market for channel engagement, compliance as competitive advantage, consumption tailwind from GST rationalisation and low inflation, and low-cost cross-sell through installed base.

Consolidated revenue from operations for the quarter ended 30 June 2026 was more than double that of the corresponding quarter of the previous year, while the loss for the quarter reduced to less than half the comparable level.

Credit Risk: The credit risk is the risk of financial loss to the Company if a customer or counterparty to financial instrument fails to meet its contractual obligations, and arises principally from the Company's receivables from customers and investments in debt securities.
Liquidity Risk: Liquidity risk is the risk that Company may not be able to meet its present and future cash and collateral obligations without incurring unacceptable losses.

Market Risk: Market risk is the risk that the fair value of future cash flows of a financial instrument will fluctuate because of changes in market prices. Financial instruments affected by market risk include loans borrowings and deposits.
Interest rate risk: The Company's exposures to the risk of changes in market interest rates relates primarily to the Company's long term debt obligation with floating interest rates.
